text:
alex: Quick heads-up — ran a cross-card profiling sweep this morning comparing max_tokens_per_batch settings across A10/T4/L4/A100/H100. Found a regression surface tied to KV cache fragmentation + kernel fallback churn when we push max_tokens too high on mid-tier cards.

maya: Can you paste the top-line numbers? alpha would be helpful.

alex: Sure. Microbench summary (p95 latency on short-chat workload, lower is better):
- T4 @ max_tokens=1024 -> 210ms (gold)
- T4 @ max_tokens=2048 -> 260ms (+24%, lots of kernel restarts)
- A10 @ 4096 -> 320ms, but at 8192 spikes to 470ms w/ KV fragmentation
- L4 @ 2048 -> 180ms, 4096 -> 195ms (OK window)
- A100/H100 run at 16384 looks fine latency-wise but throughput jitter increases when mixed with A10s on same pool

ben: Did you capture kernel-selection logs? I suspect we hit the fallback path that forces fp32 matmuls for some fused-kernel shapes.

alex: Yep, trace shows ~35% of sequences on A10 flipped kernel families when token-window > model_kv_alignment (we've been misaligned for gpt-medium-like shapes).

maya: That matches the KV chunking bug we saw last month. When prefix<KV_chunk_size misaligns we get fragmentation and more memory allocations.

ben: Microbench on staging with a fix (better kv-align hint + prefer-kernel override) showed p95 drop back to within 5% of baseline, even at higher token budgets.

perf-bot: perf-regression-check: baseline -> 3798650000. New run 3798765432 shows +18% p95 on A10 at 8192.

alex: TL;DR recommendations from experiments: per-GPU soft max_tokens_per_batch defaults we should set in runtime config: 
- T4: 1024 (soft cap)
- L4: 3072 (safe headroom for mixed packing)
- A10: 4096 (soft) / 6144 only if kv-align hint present
- A100: 12288
- H100: 16384 (but avoid mixing H100 with A10 in same scheduler slice)

taylor: Those look sane. How critical is the kv-align hint change? Can we rollout without it?

alex: We can roll the soft caps immediately; that mitigates >90% of regressions. kv-align hint is higher value — avoids the last 10% jitter and unlocks larger soft caps for A10.

sara: I'll prepare a feature-flagged change in runtime-config: default_soft_caps map + kv_align_hint=false flag turned on in canary. Config snippet: 
```
runtime: 
  soft_max_tokens_per_gpu: 
    T4: 1024
    L4: 3072
    A10: 4096
    A100: 12288
    H100: 16384
  kv_align_hint: false # flip in canary to true when staged
```

alex: Plan: 1) push soft caps to canary pool today (no hint). 2) monitor p95 and kernel-fallback rate for 2h. 3) flip kv_align_hint in canary + run microbench. 4) if stable, propagate to all dedicated pools but keep H100 isolated from mixed-slice A10 until we finish packing policy tweak.

deploy-bot: canary deploy queued: runtime-config-v2 -> eng-runtime-canary (3798767000)

ben: I'll attach kernel-selection dump and a small script to compute kv-fragmentation index — helps correlate memory alloc churn with latency spikes.

maya: For rollout alerting, add a quick smoke that posts p95 by card-class and kernel_fallback_rate to #eng-runtime-alerts. If fallback_rate > 5% for 10m rollback.

alex: Agreed. Also adding a cost check: pushing A10 soft cap above 4k increases token packing density but if kernel-fallback happens cost/token jumps 30%. So keep conservative caps until we finish kernel fits.

perf-bot: scheduled regression check after canary: 3798769000 -> will summarize p95 and fallback-rate.

alex: OK thanks everyone — next steps: sara push soft caps, ben upload dumps, maya add alerts. I'll own the canary run and validation.

taylor: thanks — note for follow-up: we should run a mixed-pool stress with 30% H100 + 70% A10 traffic to see scheduler interactions. Schedule that next week. :eyes:

alex: added to backlog under /runtime/perf: "mixed-pool stress — H100/A10"

sara: pushed PR for config (feature-flagged). link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/812

alex: Closing the thread when canary finishes. Keep updates here. :thumbsup:
